:JUDGMENT:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.15,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 30012019 at about 11.30 a.m., when the Petitioner was riding a Yamaha Fascino scooter bearing No.KA 05KJ3532 and when she reached near Nallur gate, on MulabagalKolar NH75 road, Mulabagal Taluk, Kolar District, at that time,
a bus bearing Regn.No.KA06C3546 driven by its driver came from same direction in a rash and negligent manner, lost control over the vehicle, went to wrong side of the road and dashed violently against the Petitioner's scooter from behind and caused the accident.
Due to the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to R.L.Jalappa Hospital, Kolar, wherein, she took treatment as an inpatient.

He spent Rs.1,00,000/
towards treatment, conveyance and nourishments and other incidental charges.
Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and she was working as a tailor and homemaker and was earning Rs.25,000/ per month.
Due to the accident, she has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.

The Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending bus and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the bus and therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
3. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 and Respondent No.2 appeared before the court through their counsels and filed objections to the main petition.

The Respondent No.1 in his Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending bus.
Further denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and the expenses incurred for the medical treatment.
Hence, among these and other grounds, Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against him.
The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement has denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of bus.
Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and the expenses incurred for the medical treatment.

Further, it contended that the driver of the offending bus does Smt.Varalakshmi.S.N vs Mr.Afsar Pasha on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66065340/
2 not possess Driving licence at the time of accident.
Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation.
Hence, among these and other grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
4. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 30.01.2019 at about 11.30 a.m. near Nallur gate, on Mulabagal Kolar NH75 road,
Mulabagal Taluk, Kolar District, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of bus bearing No. KA06C3546?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?

If so, how much and from whom?
3.
What Order
or Award ?
5. In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 8 documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.8 and closed her side evidence.

On the other hand,
Respondent No.2 examined ARTO as RW.1 and got marked 2 documents as per Ex.R.1 and R.2 and it also examined two other witnesses as RW.2 and RW.3 and got marked 6 documents as Ex.R.3 to R.8 and closed its side evidence.
Respondent No.1 did not choose to lead evidence.
6. The Learned Counsel for the Petitioner has relied on the following citations.

1. MFA.No.8825/2015 (MV) (Sri.Raghavendra.S Vs. Munesh and others)
2. 2020 ACJ 1055(KAR) (S.N.Kenchanna Vs. Anitha & Others)
3. 2020 ACJ 267 (KAR) ( Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Jayamma and others) The Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 has relied on the following citations.

7. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record and the citations relied on by the learned counsel for Petitioner and Respondent No.2, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No. 2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order Smt.Varalakshmi.S.N vs Mr.Afsar Pasha on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66065340/
3  for the following :

REASONS 8. Issue No. 1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that she had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic accident that occurred on 30012019 at about 11.30 a.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the bus bearing Regn.No.KA06C3546.
9.
On the other hand, the Respondents have denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending bus.
10. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, she got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked 8 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P8.
P.W.1 has reiterated the Petition averments in her chief affidavit.
Ex.P1 to Ex.P5 are the True copies of FIR with Complaint, Spot Panchanama, IMV report, Wound certificate and Charge sheet.
Ex.P.6 is the Discharge summary, Ex.P.7 is the Medical bills and Ex.P.8 is the Prescriptions.

11. Upon going through Ex.P1, it shows that on the complaint lodged by the Petitioner before Mulabagal Rural Police Station, the PSI of the concerned Police Station has registered the case against the driver of the bus bearing Reg.No.KA06C3546 for the offences punishable under Sec.
279, 337 of IPC.
Ex.P2 is the Spot Panchanama which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P.3 is the IMV report which shows that the accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defect of the motor vehicles.
Ex.P4 is the Wound Certificate in respect of the Petitioner which shows that the Petitioner had sustained grievous and simple injuries.

Ex.P5 is the Certified copy of the Charge sheet which shows that after thorough investigation, the PSI of Mulbagal Rural Police Station has submitted Chargesheet against the driver of the offending bus for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 338 of IPC and under Section 192(A) of IMV Act.

12. Upon going through the Chargesheet i.e., Ex.P5 Column No.17 reads as under:
" 30012019    1130       12        ...    KA06C3546         ..75            
    Yamaha Fasino   KA 05 KJ 3532    1  ..  
     ,   
,  ,  ,   
 ...   KA 06 C 3546         ..75          .

4      ,   
  ..75     ,  
   ."
13. Further, P.W.1 examined Dr.Pradeep.Y.V as P.W.2 and he also reiterated about the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a RTA.
14. To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 has cross examined the P.W.1.
In the crossexamination P.W.1 has denied the suggestions of the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.1 and 2 and nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of the Petitioner.
15. To rebut the evidence of PW.1, Respondent No.2 has examined three witnesses as RW.1 to RW.3 and got marked 8 documents at Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.8.
But, nothing could be elicited in their evidence to disbelieve the version of the Petitioner.
Moreover, the Charge sheet is the material document which is filed against the driver of the offending bus and the said charge sheet is not challenged by the driver of the offending bus.

16. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the depositions and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending bus and in the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No. 1 in the 'Affirmative'.
17. Issue No. 2 : As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending bus by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
18. In the petition, the Petitioner has shown her age as 31 years.
She has not produced any document to prove her age.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner as on the date of accident was 31 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
19. Further, the Petitioner has averred that she was working as Tailor and housewife and was earning Rs.25,000/ per month.
In this regard, she has not produced any document to prove her income.

Therefore, in the absence of proof of income, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e., Rs.14,000/p.m. as the accident has been occurred in the year of 2019, for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
20. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
21.
The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P4 and other medical records reveals that in the accident the Petitioner has sustained following injuries;
1. Closed undisplaced fracture of left distal end radius.

Mr.Afsar Pasha

5
2. Closed displaced fracture of bone of proximal phalanx of left 5th finger.
3. Lacerated wound of 4 x 5 cm. of left forehead.
Further, the Doctor has opined that Injury No.1 and 2 are grievous in nature and Injury No.3 is simple in nature..

Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

I COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
22.
Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
23.

The Petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in her evidence that she was admitted as an inpatient from 30.01.2019 to 09.02.2019 at R.L.Jalappa Hospital,
Kolar.
Upon going through Ex.P.6 i.e., the Discharge summary which shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient from 30.01.2019 to 09.02.2019 i.e., totally for 10 days.
Therefore, the total period which the petitioner was admitted as inpatient is 10 days.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.28,000/ under this head (@ Rs.14,000/ per month ).

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
24.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also she might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for her conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/ towards attendants charges, Rs.6,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,000/ under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :

25. The Petitioner has deposed that she spent more than  1,00,000/ towards medical expenses Smt.Varalakshmi.S.N vs Mr.Afsar Pasha on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66065340/
6 and other expenses.
In order to prove this fact, she has produced 22 medical bills i.e., Ex.P.7 which is totally amounting to Rs.29,520/.
I have gone through the medical bills and the same are acceptable.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.29,600/as a compensation under this head.

VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :
26.
The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by her in the accident, she has suffered permanent disablement and she cannot lift, carry or bear any weight with left upper limb.
She cannot lift and rotate her hand and lost grip and grasp in left hand.
Even in her evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.
However, Petitioner has neither examined any doctor to prove her disability nor she has produced any disability certificate from competent authority.
Therefore, the Petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future earning capacity due to permanent disability.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
27.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 50,000/
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 40,000/
3. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 18,000/ diet, and conveyance 4.

Medical expenses Rs. 29,600/
5. Loss of income during the Rs. 28,000/ laid up period 6. Loss of Future income
Total Rs.1,65,600/

Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.1,65,600/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a.
from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

28. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA 06C3546.

It is the contention of the Respondent No.2 that on the alleged date, the driver of the offending bus had driven the same without having valid and effective Driving licence and the bus had no valid permit to ply on the accident place route.
In order to prove the said contention, the Respondent No.2 examined 3 witnesses as RW.1 to 3 and got marked in total 8 documents at Ex.R.1 to R.8.
RW.1 is Nayaz Pasha, ARTO, KGF, Bangalore has deposed
that, the driver of the offending bus had Driving licence to ride two wheeler and LMV vehicle which is valid from 14.08.2013 to 13.08.2033.

Further, he deposed that the said driver Ayub Khan did not possess Driving licence to drive bus and Transport vehicles.
He got marked the Authorisation Letter as per Ex.R.1 and true copy of Driving licence of Ayub Khan at Ex.R.2.
Further he deposed that as per Ex.R.2, the driver did not possess badge and as on 30.01.2019, he did not possess Driving licence to drive bus.
In the cross examination he denied the suggestions.
The Respondent No.2 also examined one Kiran Kumar, SDC at RTO as RW.2 and he deposed that Permit of the offending bus was renewed from 31.03.2016 to 30.03.2021.
The said Route Permit was given to travel from Jigani to Chikkathirupathi and the said bus is Stage Carrier bus.
Further he deposed that as per the said permit, the stage bus does not had Permit to travel from Mulbagilu to Kolar.
Further, he got marked Authorisation Letter as per Ex.R.3 and Endorsement of Replacement and Endorsement of Renewal of Permit and Route Permit as per Ex.R.4 to R.6.
In the cross examination, he deposed that he does not know whether RTO taken action against the said offending bus for violation of Route Permit.
The Respondent No.2 also examined its Administrative Officer (Legal) by name Bikram Singh as RW.3 and he has reiterated the Objection statement contentions in his chief affidavit.
Further he got marked two documents at Ex.R.7 and R.8 i.e., Authorisation letter and copy of the Insurance policy.
In the cross examination, he denied the suggestions.
Upon going through the Charge sheet i.e., Ex.P.5, I.O also mentioned Section 192(A) of IMV Act for violation of Route Permit.
Admittedly, the said accident was occurred near Nellur gate on MulbagiluKolar NH75 road.
As per the evidence of RW.2, the offending bus had Route Permit to travel from Jigani to Chikkatirupathi and it does not had Permit to travel from Mulbagilu to Kolar.

It is also admitted fact that, on the date of accident, it has deviated from its route.

The recent decisions in which the Learned Counsel for Petitioner was relied on clearly shows that our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has pleased to held that violation of Route Permit was not resulted in exoneration of the liability of the insurance company.
It is further contention of the Respondent No.2 that on the alleged date, the driver of the offending bus did not possess valid and effective Driving licence.

In order to support the contention of the Respondent No.2, it has examined ARTO, KGF as RW.1 and in the evidence of RW.1, he has deposed that on the date of accident, the driver of the offending bus did not possess Driving licence to drive the bus.
Further, he deposed that the driver of the offending bus possessed Driving licence to ride two wheeler and LMV vehicles.
Further he got marked Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2 i.e., copy of Authorisation Letter and Extract of Driving licence.
It shows that the driver of the offending vehicle possessed Driving licence to drive the LMV vehicle (Non Transport) from 14.08.2013 to 13.08.2033.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".

29. Point No. 3 : In view of my findings on Points No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER

The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents U/Sec.
166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of Rs.1,65,600/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.

However, the Respondent No.2 being the Insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award and then recover the same from the Respondent No.1 through due process of law.

On deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, since the same is meager one, the entire amount shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E Payment after her proper identification.

The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs. 1000/.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.15,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic accident.
Due to the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
He spent Rs.1,00,000/
towards treatment, conveyance and nourishments and other incidental charges.
Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and she was working as a tailor and homemaker and was earning Rs.25,000/ per month.
Due to the accident, she has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.
The Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending bus and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the bus and therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.1 in his Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending bus.
Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.28,000/ under this head (@ Rs.14,000/ per month ).
In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/ towards attendants charges, Rs.6,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,000/ under this head.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.29,600/as a compensation under this head.
To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 50,000/
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 40,000/
3. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 18,000/ diet, and conveyance 4.
Medical expenses Rs. 29,600/
5. Loss of income during the Rs. 28,000/ laid up period 6. Loss of Future income
Therefore, Respondent No.1 is liable to pay compensation amount to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
29. Point No. 3 : In view of my findings on Points No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents U/Sec.
166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of Rs.1,65,600/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.2 being the Insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award and then recover the same from the Respondent No.1 through due process of law.
On deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, since the same is meager one, the entire amount shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E Payment after her proper identification.
